ArthaInvest — Prospecting Dashboard

The diagnosis

What the numbers say when you put them next to each other.

You do not have a lead shortage. 11,466 contactable people produced a 12-row pipeline and 27 clients. The constraint is triage and follow-up, not volume — which is why the cold list gets cut to 120 and the client book comes first.
Every dated record is 2018, 2020 or 2021 — nothing since. The files were last touched in early 2024. Mining this database is a one-off harvest, not a pipeline. Expect heavy phone disconnection on 5–8 year old numbers; that is normal, not a bad list.
The staleness helps for loans. Someone who bought in Feb 2021 is ~5.5 years into a 20-year loan right now — the balance-transfer and top-up window. That is where the ₹39.8cr confirmed-buyer loan book comes from.

Work these in order

Warmest first. Do not start at the big list — start at the top of this page.

1 · Live enquiries — people who already asked you about a loan. Warmest intent on file, and the shortest conversation. 2 · Confirmed buyers — you know they bought, what they paid and when. 3 · Tier A — scored on provable income and collateral, not wealth.
Before dialling: DND-scrub the numbers, keep to 09:00–21:00, and never promise approval, a rate or a saving — the lender decides. These numbers are 5–8 years old, so expect heavy disconnection. That is normal, not a bad list.

1 · Live loan enquiries

They raised a loan requirement with you already. Call these first.

2 · Confirmed buyers — ₹39.8cr of loan book in play

Booked February 2021, paid only ₹50k–₹5L upfront — the rest was financed. At ~5.5 years into a 20-year term, this is the balance-transfer and top-up window.

3 · Tier A loan prospects

Scored differently to the investment list: salaried with a named employer beats a wealthy business owner, because loans are approved on documentable income.

Requirement mix

The same database, cut by who people are

Work one segment at a time rather than the whole list at once.

These are not new names — every one is already in the master database. Apollo and similar B2B tools sell work emails and job titles for selling software to companies; they hold no individual wealth data, so they cannot supply this ICP. HubSpot is a CRM — somewhere to put leads, not a source of them.

UHNI — ₹8cr+ budget

HNI — ₹4–8cr budget

Your best-converting segment and the least competitive. You already hold the FATCA and NRI KYC forms.

Doctors & medical

Use the MedMoney deck. Referral-dense communities.

Bank employees

Worth approaching twice over — as clients, and because bank staff are how the SCB/DBS referral channel started. These are not your referring RMs; those names are in your phone, not in any file.

The single highest-leverage cluster

Where one conversation reaches many people — which is what matters when you are part-time.

BARC — 16 prospects, and "Anushakti Nagar" in your top localities. That is one employer and one residential colony: salaried government scientists, documentable income, stable employment, living in the same place. It is the best single target in the database for a FinRakshak session — one room, many first-party consented leads, and the DPDP problem disappears because they hand you their details directly.
Banking cluster worth noting: Kotak, HDFC, Axis and Morgan Stanley appear together. Finance employees are an easy audience for tax-regime and NPS conversations — and they refer well internally.

START HERE — 120 Tier A prospects with an email

Email first so the opening touch carries an unsubscribe. About 8 weeks at 15/week.

These came from a third party with no consent chain. First touch asks permission and does not pitch; two touches maximum, then permanent suppression. See the compliance doc.

220 brokers — the fix for stale data

Not retail prospects. A referral channel that produces fresh leads indefinitely.

Brokers close deals every month, and every buyer needs a home loan that month. A 2021 lead list is a harvest; a broker channel is an annuity. You do not need 220 — you need 5 who actually send you business.

People you actually know

From three phone books: your own, Hitesh (partner) and Manohar Arora (family).

These can't be scored — they have to be recognised. 96% carry only a name and a number, so there's nothing in the data to rank on. The qualification is in your head, or Hitesh's. Search for a name you remember rather than reading top to bottom.
Who introduces matters. Your own contacts you approach directly. Hitesh's contacts convert far better if he introduces you, or you open with "Hitesh and I work together". Same for Manohar's. A cold call to someone who has no idea who you are wastes the relationship that made them warm.
Excluded automatically: — family and relationship labels, household trades (plumber, carpenter, driver, maid), helplines and boss entries. Nothing was deleted; the full excluded list is the second sheet of 14_Warm_Network.xlsx if you want to review it.

Before you contact anyone

DND-scrub before calling — emails are fine, calls to DND-registered numbers are not. Never promise a return on investments, or approval/rate/saving on a loan — the lender decides. Log every opt-out in suppression_list.csv immediately, and never contact them again.

Who's using this dashboard?

This is workflow separation, not security. A local file cannot authenticate anyone — whoever holds this file can read all of it. Real access control is who you share the OneDrive folder with. Client data is personal data: only give it to people who need it.
